Article Title: At least 2 killed, nine injured in reactor blast at Telangana pharma unit
Article Text:
Reactor blast at Telangana pharma unit

Two workers were killed and nine others injured after a reactor blast triggered a fire at a pharmaceutical unit in Telangana's Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district late Friday night, police said.The incident took place at a pharma company in Pochampally mandal while workers were changing shifts, according to police."Two persons died. Nine people were injured, including two who suffered more than 50 per cent burns while seven sustained minor injuries", a police official told PTI.The injured workers were admitted to different hospitals for treatment, the official said.The blast triggered a fire at the unit, which was later brought under control by the Fire Department.Police have registered a case and launched an investigation into the incident.
Article Summary: Reactor blast at telangana pharma unit kills two workers, injures nine others. Incident took place at a pharma company in pochampally mandal while workers were changing shifts. Police have registered a case and launched an investigation into the incident.

Article Title: Gateways to a thousand worlds
Article Text: Thirukkural with the Times explores real-world lessons from the classic Tamil text ‘Thirukkural’. Written by Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, the Kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each. This text is divided into three books with teachings on virtue, wealth, and love and is considered one of the great works ever on ethics and morality. The Kural has influenced scholars and leaders across social, political, and philosophical spheres.Motivational speaker, author and diversity champion Bharathi Bhaskar explores the masterpiece.Recently, I was invited to address a meeting at the Gopala Rao Public Library in Kumbakonam. More than 136 years old, it houses over 70,000 books, many more than a century old including original commentaries on the Thirukkural to the first publication of Tagore’s Gitanjali, in his own handwriting in Bengali, and an English translation by Tagore himself, with a foreword by W B Yeats.Walking among the old books, I was taken back to my school years when I was a voracious reader.We lived in Thiruvallikeni, Chennai, and I craved books; having read every book at home a hundred times. My mother began sending me with my elder sister to old newspaper shops. We would rummage through discarded books and return home delighted with our treasures. My mother also got me memberships in two libraries . One was the prestigious Kasthuri Srinivasan Library. Entering it was soul-stirring. I would scan the shelves for unread books, careful to return them on time. The second was a govt-sponsored bus converted into a library. Once, when the bus was preparing to leave, I pleaded with the driver, “Anna, please, five more minutes!” I wanted to finish the book I was reading .Books held a special place in our lives. We did not merely read a book; we entered a different world. Sitting in a chair at home, I rode the horse with Vandhiyathevan in Ponniyin Selvan, sat beside Ganesh and Vasanth, the charming lawyers from Sujatha’s stories, and travelled through the worlds of Irving Wallace, Jeffrey Archer and attended the court rooms with Perry Mason.Libraries have always been more than buildings because knowledge is the root of a culture. And history shows us why those who seek to erase a culture have so often attacked its libraries. The Serapeum of Alexandria, the library with pagan literature on palm leaves, was destroyed in 391 AD, as part of the suppression of pagan institutions under Emperor Theodosius I. Nalanda’s great library complex was destroyed during Bakhtiyar Khalji’s invasion; accounts describe its manuscripts burning for months. In 1981, the Jaffna Public Library, one of Asia’s largest repositories of Tamil literature, was deliberately set ablaze; its destruction widely regarded as cultural erasure .Andrew Carnegie, the prominent American industrialist spent his youth in poverty, and it was a local colonel who gave him free access to books. He later donated 40 million dollars for the construction of 2,500 public libraries in America.That is why Gopal Rao Library moved me so deeply. Will libraries become obsolete in the age of AI? Devices give us access to millions of books, but can they give us the experience of sitting quietly with one?Reading does not merely gather knowledge; it nourishes imagination, calms the mind and opens new vistas. A machine can give us an answer. A book can give us a world.Valluvar understood the joy centuries ago. In Kural 783, he says:“Navilthorum Noolnayam Polum PayilthorumPanbudai Yalar Thodarbu.”“Just as a good book gives greater delight each time it is read, the friendship of the virtuous grows sweeter with familiarity.”I hope the shelves of libraries never fall silent, the pages never stop turning, and the child in us never stops whispering —“Just one more book.”
Article Summary: Thirukkural with the times explores real-world lessons from the classic tamil text. Written by tamil poet and philosopher thiruvalluvar, the kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each. This text is divided into three books with teachings on virtue, wealth, and love.

Article Title: 105, not out? SC orders release of murder convict
Article Text:
SC permanently releases 105-year-old life convict Rasik Mandal, says he should spend his remaining days with family

Born in 1920 when Congress had launched the non-cooperation movement against the British, Rasik Mandal got his freedom as a 105-year-old life convict Friday after SC ordered the centenarian should spend his remaining days with his family. He was convicted in 1994 for a 1988 murder. On Friday, the bench first asked: "Is he alive? Why should he not be released permanently? Why should he be on interim parole?"Born in a nondescript village of Malda district, Rasik Chandra was arrested in 1988 for murder at the age of 68, and convicted in Dec 1994.His appeal against conviction was dismissed by Calcutta HC in 2018, after 24 years, and Supreme Court rejected his appeal in 2019.Serving a life sentence, he was shifted to a correctional home at Balurghat in West Bengal from prison due to age-related ailments. Mandal, through his son, had filed a writ petition in SC in 2020, when he was just short of the century-mark, seeking premature release on ground of age and related ailments. On Nov 29, 2024, SC admitted Mandal’s petition and directed his release “on interim bail/parole in the case lodged on Nov 9, 1988, at Manikchak police station in WB’s Malda”.On Friday, as the Supreme Court bench wondered why he should not be released, the West Bengal counsel said the court could direct that he would not be incarcerated any longer. “Having regard to his age, we see no reason not to release him. We allow his writ petition while making the Nov 29, 2024, order absolute. He is permanently released from jail for the purpose of this case,” the apex court said.
Article Summary: Sc permanently releases 105-year-old life convict rasik mandal, says he should spend his remaining days with family. He was convicted in 1994 for a 1988 murder. Mandal, through his son, had filed a writ petition in sc in 2020, when he was just short of the century mark.

Article Title: Fadnavis letter: SG flags power tribunal to CJI
Article Text:
SG Tushar Mehta asks CJI Surya Kant to examine APTEL’s functioning after Maharashtra govt flags alleged pro-private power developer bias

New Delhi: Days after Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis flagged pro-private power developer bias of Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) in a letter to PM Narendra Modi, solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta on Friday requested CJI Surya Kant to look into the tribunal's functioning.While seeking an urgent hearing of an appeal filed by Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC) against JSW Energy Ltd, Mehta said: "The CJI must examine what is happening in APTEL." MERC has challenged APTEL's decision not to send the case back to the state regulator for fresh consideration.MERC said, “The manner in which APTEL has proceeded in deciding MERC’s appeal is egregious as it has summarily dismissed the submissions of the regulator” and wrongly recorded that Solicitor General had made no attempt to take the tribunal through the impugned order or explain why the regulator considered the order to be erroneous and in need of reconsideration.MERC added , “During the course of the arguments, the SG had taken APTEL through the notification as well as the impugned order in detail. Specific arguments were advanced regarding inherent lack of jurisdiction as well as the error apparent on the face of the record.”There was a dispute between Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Co (MSEDC) and JSW over applicability of central govt’s May 5, 2022, notification on operation at full capacity of imported coal-based power plants.On Dec 24 2025, MERC said that since JSW is an intra-state power plant, the notification would not apply to it making Power Purchase Agreement rates applicable.MSEDC challenged MERC’s order before APTEL. During the pendency of the appeal, MERC felt it had committed a jurisdictional error on applicability of the central notification and wanted to revisit its decision. It requested APTEL to remit the matter back for reconsideration, which was refused on Aug 19.MERC said, “APTELheld that the Commission’s request for reconsideration of the matter was intriguing and insinuated that the same was an attempt to aid MSEDC in forum shopping.”Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis cited several examples of arbitrary adverse treatment of public utilities by APTEL and requested PM to order an examination of the tribunal’s functioning to ensure that justice is delivered and interests of govt companies are protected.
Article Summary: Sg tushar mehta asks cji surya kant to examine aptel’s functioning after maharashtra govt flags alleged pro-private power developer bias. There was a dispute between maharashtra state electricity distribution co (msedc) and jsw over applicability of central govt's may 5, 2022 notification.

Article Title: HC questions ED move to keep case alive even after FIR closure
Article Text:
Delhi HC quashes ED proceedings, says agency cannot continue PMLA probe after closure of underlying FIR

NEW DELHI: Delhi HC has taken a dim view of ED 's move to rely on a six-year-old case to continue proceedings even though the FIR forming the basis of the case was closed. Justice Anish Dayal observed that despite being aware that the original FIR stood closed, ED's was attempting to "somehow preserve the existing ECIR" and retain the coercive powers under PMLA with respect to search, seizure, freezing and attachment of properties of the petitioners."The conduct of the ED in this regard is found wanting and raises serious concerns," the high court observed in a recent judgement.ED's ECIR, registered in Dec 2021, arose from an FIR registered by Economic Offences Wing (EOW) in Feb 2021 over a dispute between two factions of the family of the late Mahendra Prasad, a former MP. The issue pertained to share transfers and bank transactions by a faction of the family on the basis of forged signatures of Prasad's wife.In Dec 2022, EOW, however, filed a cancellation report upon completion of the investigation, saying no offence was made out.However, in 2019, another FIR was registered alleging wrongful confinement of the ex-MP's wife, removal of certain jewellery and offences under the Passports Act, which was cited by ED to carry on its PMLA probe.The court said an ECIR depended upon existence of a predicate offence, and therefore, any action taken by ED would come to an end on the closure of the FIR on the predicate offence.HC quashed all proceedings, including coercive action taken by ED, and directed it to restore status quo ante in favour of respective petitioners. Article Title: Advocates can now apply for judge posts after 1-year practice
Article Text:
SC eases civil judge eligibility from 3-year to 1-year practice, but mandates 2 years of training before judges can preside over courts

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The 20-year-old method for recruiting entry-level trial court judges underwent changes twice in one year as the Supreme Court on Friday relaxed mandatory three-year practice eligibility norm for advocates to apply for judicial officer posts to one-year practice but said they can preside over courts and decide cases only after a two year on-job training.The SC in 1993 had ordered that advocates with three-year practice alone would be eligible to take the tests for posts of civil judges and magistrates. But in 2002, the SC had reversed its decision allowing fresh law graduates to become entry level judicial officers. Significantly, the law commission in 1986 had said fresh law graduates may take the test for judicial officers, but on being successful should take two years intensive on-job training.Making a mixture out of the three-decade spanning endeavour to make judicial officers competent and capable to decide cases, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices A G Masih and Vinod Chandran by two to one majority, Justice Chandran dissenting, said lawyers with one year practice would be eligible to appear in the three-layered examination for judicial officer selection.As most HCs favoured retaining the three-year practice eligibility criteria on the ground that fresh law graduates with no exposure to judicial proceedings were found wanting in their behaviour in courtroom and handling of sensitive cases, SC provided a new eligibility criteria with mandatory two-year training period for every advocate who clears the recruitment process.CJI Kant and Justice Masih in the majority judgement said law graduates with one year practice can apply for the posts of judicial officers. On getting selected, they will be designated as 'Trainee Judicial Officers" and "shall undergo a compulsory period of one year of intensive training at the State Judicial Academy concerned" and will be paid a fixed emolument equivalent to half the salary of magistrates. After one year training, the trainee judicial officers would undergo one year structured law clerkship - six months with the principal district judge and the next six months will be with a sitting HC judge, who will give a report evaluating the performance and suitability of the trainee.
Article Summary: Sc eases civil judge eligibility from 3-year to 1-year practice, but mandates 2 years of training before judges can preside over courts. In 2002, the sc had reversed its decision allowing fresh law graduates to become entry level judicial officers.

Former Union minister and senior Congress leader P Chidambaram said on Friday that the party wants the existing allocation of Lok Sabha seats to be maintained for another 25 years, with no change to the current strength of 543 seats or Tamil Nadu’s 39 constituencies.Chidambaram added that the resolutions passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and the Congress Working Committee on delimitation reflected the same position.“The resolutions passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and the Congress Working Committee regarding the delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies reflect the same stance. There should be no change to the current Lok Sabha strength of 543 seats or Tamil Nadu’s allocation of 39 constituencies. The Congress party’s position is that the current seat allocations should be maintained for another 25 years,” Chidambaram said in a post on X.“It is gratifying that both the ruling party (TVK) and the principal opposition party (DMK) in Tamil Nadu support this stance,” he added.The development comes a day after Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay raised concerns over the proposed Delimitation Bill, 2026, warning that southern states could lose parliamentary representation if seats are redistributed primarily on the basis of population.Speaking at the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council chaired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday, Vijay, who is also the council’s vice-chairman, sought an assurance from the Centre that states that had successfully stabilised their populations would not be penalised through a reduction in their parliamentary representation.He said the issue had assumed importance as the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census approaches its end."As the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census approaches its end and the Delimitation Bill, 2026, is considered, there is a genuine and shared concern across the Southern States that delimitation based predominantly on populations may diminish our collective voice in Parliament," he said.Vijay said southern states had successfully controlled population growth while making progress in human development and economic growth. He argued that these achievements should not lead to a reduction in their political representation.The Tamil Nadu Assembly had earlier passed a special resolution urging the Centre to permanently retain the Lok Sabha’s strength at 543 seats.The government-sponsored resolution also called for the 33 per cent reservation for women to be implemented in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections without delay, based on the existing strength of 543 seats.
Article Summary: Former union minister and senior congress leader p chidambaram said on friday that the party wants the existing allocation of lok sabha seats to be maintained for another 25 years. Article Title: SC faults UP Gangsters Act, says it is prone to misuse
Article Text:
SC flags ‘serious flaws’ in UP Gangsters Act, warns of misuse against innocents

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Pointing out various flaws in Uttar Pradesh Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, Supreme Court on Thursday said the law is prone to misuse as there is no safeguard against vindictive and malicious action against innocents.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the special Act does not create any offence, which is the requirement of any penal law. "But for the definition clause, defining 'gang' and 'gangster', there is no offence insofar as the membership in the gang or acting in cohort with a gang, either singly or together," it said."The subject enactment, the UP Act not only permits detention for a period without anything more than the inclusion in a Gang Chart but also enables a trial and punishment on the basis of the very same Gang Chart, in addition to the pre-trial incarceration, but without an offence being created by the Act itself. It is akin to the English proverb: Give a dog a bad name and hang him," the bench said.Observing that the UP law fails to satisfy judicial conscience, SC said menace of criminal gangs is to be curbed, but the end does not justify the means, especially in enacting a penal law that interferes with liberty of citizens.The apex court was particularly concerned about two issues - "(1) the total absence of creation of a crime, which is mandatory in a penal statute and (2) the punishment being imposed on a status determined for a person, that too on the whim of the administrative officers and police personnel by preparation of a Gang Chart under the Rules, not specifically provided under the statute.""We cannot but observe, with respect, that there is always a tendency among the wisest of men to label a question; to which they find no answer or a difficult or unpalatable one, as foolish and the one who raised it, a fool," the bench said."We hence, endeavoured to find an answer to the two questions we have posed above, by posing it to the learned Counsel appearing for the State. We did so, at the risk of being called foolhardy and our only solace is that the very same questions were raised before the full bench of the Allahabad high court, at that juncture, but by wise men, eminent lawyers of considerable repute," it said.SC said the counsel appearing for the state neither could give an answer at the time of arguments nor attempted to do so in the written submissions placed before the court.The SC bench said the provisions of the Act could lead to detention of the accused without trial for long, which is akin to a statute enjoining preventive detention, and there is no safeguard against such preventive detention."However compelling the social menace, any penal enactment cannot lead to arbitrary actions. A mere allegation can trigger a gang chart, arrest and year-long remand. There is no safeguard against vindictive and malicious action against 'the innocent, the righteous, the virtuous, a whistleblower'," it said.
Article Summary: Sc flags ‘serious flaws’ in up gangsters act, warns of misuse against innocents. Justices j b pardiwala and k vinod chandran said the special act does not create any offence, which is the requirement of any penal law.

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Friday hit back at the Congress after several of its leaders paid tribute to former party leader Sajjan Kumar, a convict in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, who died at 80 Congress MP Deepender Hooda described the death of Kumar, a former three-term Lok Sabha MP, as an "irreparable loss.""Today, the country's political landscape has suffered an irreparable loss... Sajjan Kumar ji was a leader whose connection with people in Delhi and across north India was cited as a model across the country," he said.Reacting to Hooda's remarks, BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress of "eulogising the killers of the Sikh community", referring to Kumar's role in the anti-Sikh riots."Congress calls late Sajjan Kumar, a man convicted in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, a 'role model'! How can Congress eulogise the killers of our Sikh community?" Bhandari posted on X."This is the real mindset of 'Mohabbat Ki Dukkan' (shop of love) of Rahul Gandhi and exposes the innate hate Congress has for the Sikh community!" Bhandari added, referring to a phrase used by Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha.The BJP spokesperson further demanded that Congress apologise for "insulting" the victims of the anti-Sikh riots and "rubbing" salt into the wounds of the survivors and victims' families.Congress leader Udit Raj also described Kumar's death as a "great loss" for the party."It is a great loss for the Congress. He was a very senior Congress leader, and it will be difficult to fill the void... He did a lot of work, especially for the poor," Raj stated.Sajjan Kumar died at Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital on Thursday."Sajjan Kumar was brought to Safdarjung Hospital by police with altered sensorium around 11 am. He was immediately admitted and resuscitation measures were initiated. Despite providing all necessary medical and life-support measures, he could not be saved and passed away at 12:30 pm," the hospital's statement read."He was a known case of high blood pressure and Parkinson's disease and had a history of multiple hospital admissions in the past," the statement added.Kumar was serving multiple life sentences after his conviction in cases linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi.He was sentenced to life imprisonment by the Delhi High Court on December 17, 2018, in a case related to the killing of five Sikhs and the burning of a gurdwara during the anti-Sikh riots.He was also sentenced to life imprisonment by a Delhi court in February 2025 in another case relating to the killing of two Sikh men during the riots.Kumar resigned from the primary membership of the Congress after the 2018 conviction.

Article Title: India, Nepal to drone-map 'Dasgaja' encroachments after Balen remark row
Article Text:
(Representative image) The decision was taken at the 13th meeting of the Survey Officials Committee, led by deputy chiefs of Nepal’s Survey Department and Survey of India, in Lucknow last week (Photo: ANI)

NEW DELHI: India and Nepal have decided to use drones to map encroachments along 'Dasgaja' areas — the 10-yard no-man’s strip along the international boundary. The two countries will also look at “cross-border occupation”, where citizens of one nation farm, live on or hold land falling on the other side, across the 1,880km open border.The decision was taken at the 13th meeting of Survey Officials Committee, led by deputy chiefs of Nepal’s Survey Department and Survey of India, in Lucknow last week. Officials said the exercise will create a jointly verified technical record of affected areas, which can later help the two countries negotiate removal of encroachments, restoration of land or compensation.The issue returned to Nepal’s political centre stage after PM Balendra Shah told Parliament in May that "Nepal had also encroached on Indian land". The remark came when Shah was questioned about Limpiyadhura, Lipulekh and Kalapani — territories under India which Nepal claims as its own — and triggered opposition protests. Nepal’s foreign ministry later clarified that Shah was referring to Dasgaja encroachments and cross-border occupation, not territorial claims.Nepal Survey Department spokesperson Dayanand Joshi said, “It has been decided to map cross-border occupation using drones.”He added, “This includes cross-border occupation and also encroachment of Dasgaja.”Border expert and former Survey Department director general Buddhi Narayan Shrestha said the decision could help settle disputes that have lingered for decades. “Indian farmers have encroached on the land of Nepali farmers along the border, and Nepali farmers have also encroached on the land of Indian farmers to some extent. I call this cross-border land grabbing,” he said.Shrestha said his 2005 field study found Indian farmers occupying Nepali land at 84 locations and Nepali farmers occupying Indian land at 27 locations. He said such disputes arose where boundary pillars were missing or mistakes were made during local land use. “It will take some time for technicians from Nepal and India to compile such a list,” Shrestha said. “Once the data is in hand, the decision on how to resolve the issue should be made through negotiations by higher-level officials sitting at the table.Shrestha cited Nepal’s past border demarcation with China, where local officials from Tibet and Nepal resolved similar disputes through sale windows and compensation. He said nearly 42 per cent of the 8,553 border pillars shown on maps are yet to be installed, making drone mapping crucial for preventing village-level disputes from turning into diplomatic flashpoints.
Article Summary: India and nepal have decided to use drones to map encroachments along 'dasgaja' areas. The two countries will also look at “cross-border occupation’ across the 1,880km open border. Officials said the exercise will create a jointly verified technical record of affected areas.

Article Text:

How CJP protest surprised political parties

Congress’s course correction

NEW DELHI: The success of the student-powered Jantar Mantar protests seems to have forced political parties, on both sides of the divide, to return to the drawing board and redraw their strategies to woo the youth. The fact that CJP-led protests mobilised youth in large numbers against the government and forced Dharmendra Pradhan to resign left the opposition in a tight spot - as the students achieved what the parties couldn’t in the last 12 years.Little wonder then, the Congress Working Committee - the highest think tank of the grand old party, that met earlier this week devoted a lot of time discussing how to reclaim youth support for the party. The Congress announced a slew of measures to lead the fight for issues that have enraged the youth against the government and perhaps also the political parties.A glimpse of the new Congress strategy was visible today when Rahul Gandhi reached a police station in the national capital with a victim of a pellet gun used allegedly during the July 20 Sansad Chalo protest of the Jantar Mantar students, and sat on a dharna demanding that police lodge a complaint.Rahul’s police station protest follows Congress’s renewed pitch on youth outreach, deliberated and decided at the party’s Working Committee meeting held earlier this week. The CWC meeting, attended by the party’s top brass, finalised several steps to win the confidence of the youngsters and reclaim the opposition leadership space vis-a-vis the students.While the working committee launched a broadside against the Modi government for betraying the youth, it also finalised initiatives to win back their confidence.'Education-to-Employment Roadmap' for the youth was one of the key measures announced after the CWC meeting. The Congress has asked its four chief ministers to prepare a report on the reforms needed in the education and examination system in their respective states and submit it to Kharge within a month.Sources said Rahul Gandhi stressed that the chief ministers should prepare this report in consultation with education experts and all stakeholders. The objective of the exercise should be to improve the education and examination system in their respective states and secure the future of students.The Congress also announced plans to expand its 'Chhatron ki Goonj' programme, which has been used by Rahul Gandhi to interact with students, to nearly 800 cities across the country. This programme has already been held with reasonable success in Kota, Dehradun and Prayagraj and is scheduled in Pune this weekend.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, in his opening remarks at the CWC, set the agenda for youth outreach, accusing the Narendra Modi government of "destroying" students' future."The anger that has arisen among the youth across the country is not a sudden or one-day phenomenon. This government has never had the time to listen to them; instead, it has consistently sought temporary measures to sidestep the issues. Consequently, they have been forced to take to the streets," Kharge said in his CWC speech.The CWC passed a resolution expressing its “deep distress” over the plight of the youth and accusing the Modi government of betraying young people."Over the past decade, paper leaks have assumed epidemic proportions, with at least 152 cases of paper leaks reported since 2014. The recent cancellation and re-conduct of the NEET examination alone resulted in at least 26 student suicides, while more than 90 other students have lost their lives for similar reasons over the past five years," the CWC resolution said."Young people are bearing the greatest brunt of unemployment, and with 12 years having passed and opportunities shrinking, their circumstances continue to worsen. Unemployment among educated youth has now become a crisis of systemic government failure," it said.The CWC also strongly condemned the "arbitrary and brutal repression unleashed by the Modi government against student movements - including attacks on young women and children, the use of electric shock batons, tear gas, pellet guns and AK-47s, and the blatant censorship of voices of dissent".The CWC resolution also targeted Prime Minister Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah for staying away from Parliament and not answering questions on these alleged “serious failures.”The Congress recalibration follows the CJP protest, which started on June 6 and put all political parties in a Catch-22 situation.When the protest started, most of the mainstream parties stayed away. Then activist Sonam Wangchuk joined and amplified the agitation with an indefinite fast starting June 28. The initial days of his fast saw a largely muted response from most of the political parties.But the dynamics changed on July 20 - the opening day of the Monsoon session of Parliament - when the protesters went ahead with their “Sansad Chalo” march. The police crackdown on protesters catapulted the protest into a national concern and gave the opposition parties a weapon to attack the government.The Congress, which till then remained largely away from the CJP movement - focusing instead on Rahul Gandhi’s “Chhatron ki goonj” programme- was forced to act proactively to ensure it was not missing in action.So, on July 21, Congress leaders were invited to party president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence -- 10 Rajaji Marg -- to wish him on his birthday. Once they all assembled there, they marched to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence at Lok Kalyan Marg and staged a sit-in protest there against the alleged brutality committed against students during the Cockroach Janata Party's march to Parliament. The surprise sit-in led by Rahul, Kharge and Priyanka sent the government into a tizzy. It first tried to persuade the leaders to vacate the sensitive site. But when that did not work, police moved in to clear the protesters.This was the Congress’s first direct attempt to take a lead on the students’ protest. However, the effort fizzled out as the Modi government relented on July 25 and accepted CJP’s demand for Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.The Congress then shifted focus to the issue of police brutality against the student protesters on July 20 and trained its guns on Union home minister Amit Shah. It unleashed a relentless campaign inside and outside Parliament seeking Amit Shah’s resignation over the alleged use of pellet guns against protesters, which eventually led to the session washout.When students in Jharkhand followed the Jantar Mantar template and began a hunger strike against alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC), Rahul Gandhi went public with his support for the protesting students, despite the Congress being part of the state government.Rahul wrote a letter to Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren, a Congress ally, urging him to personally meet representatives of students protesting irregularities in state recruitment examinations and address their remaining concerns.The former Congress chief called the youth “India’s future” and said: “We owe them our solidarity and support at this moment of crisis. Please do your utmost to hear them out and take appropriate action towards the resolution of this issue."Days later, the Jharkhand government accepted most of the students’ demands, and the protest ended. It’s a different matter that the protesting students may feel high and dry as the Jharkhand high court put a stay on the government’s decision to cancel all previous competitive exams.With the CJP shifting focus on Rajasthan government schools, the state unit of the Congress was quick to react and take to the streets in support of the students. When a team of CJP was attacked outside a school, the state Congress quickly condemned the incident. Leader of opposition in state assembly Tika Ram Jully denounced the use of violence, stating that the public has a right to know the status of local educational facilities."This is wrong. I condemn this. There should be no violence. The condition of schools should come to light. There is no place for such violence in India. People must present their views in a non-violent manner. Schools are in bad condition; they want to hide it and cover up their sins. They won't be able to do it," Tika Ram Jully said.The state Congress leaders also slammed a recent state government order restricting unauthorised entry, media coverage, and filming on public school campuses, perhaps aimed at restricting the entry of CJP teams in state government schools.Now this is a clear change in stance, as far as the Congress is concerned. For those who remember, the Congress, for a long time, distanced itself from the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar.Clearly, the Congress strategy in Rajasthan is part of the party’s course correction after the Jantar Mantar episode. The Congress realises the importance of youth support and is trying to prioritise the issues that catch the imagination of young people. The CWC has laid out a roadmap for expanding the party’s GenZ outreach. The party has a government in four states, and this provides it with a great opportunity to showcase its intent in doing something different for the youth. Will they be able to do it? Well, we will have to wait and see.
Article Summary: The success of the student-powered jantar mantar protests seems to have forced political parties, on both sides of the divide, to redraw their strategies to woo the youth. The congress announced a slew of measures to lead the fight for issues that have enraged the youth against the government and perhaps also the political parties.

NEW DELHI: Construction activities in Delhi will be completely banned from December 10 to January 20 as part of the government's measures to control air pollution during the winter season, chief minister Rekha Gupta said on Friday.In a post on X, Gupta urged people to report violations, saying construction sites measuring more than 500 square metres would be monitored through the Delhi government's Dust Portal and AI-enabled cameras.“Construction will be completely banned from 10 December to 20 January. If you spot any violation, inform MCD, your MLA, or me directly,” Gupta said.Gupta said construction had continued at some sites during the previous winter despite the implementation of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), with work being carried out behind covers.“Last time, even under GRAP, some construction continued behind covers,” she said.This year, such sites will be monitored in real time through the Dust Portal and AI-enabled cameras. Alerts generated by the system will be sent to the government's Control and Command Centre, Gupta said.“Notices, warnings and fines will follow,” she wrote, urging people to “inform, tag, complain and stop them”.The Delhi government launched Dust Portal 2.0 in July to strengthen monitoring of construction and demolition sites and improve enforcement of dust pollution-control measures.The portal, developed by the Delhi Pollution Control Committee, integrates GIS mapping, live 360-degree PTZ cameras, PM10 and PM2.5 sensors and AI-based analytics to monitor compliance at construction sites measuring 500 square yards or more.The system generates yellow, orange and red alerts based on pollution levels and enables digital issuance of compliance certificates and enforcement notices when violations are detected.The upgraded portal also provides dashboards for district-wise monitoring, pollution trends and hotspot analysis.Officials and project proponents can remotely monitor construction sites through live camera feeds, sensor data and AI-generated analysis, according to news agency PTI.

Article Title: 20 Blackbucks rewilded in Banni Grasslands on India’s 80th Independence Day by Anant Ambani’s Vantara
Article Text:
Part of a wider Gujarat Native Herbivore Conservation Programme

On India’s 80th Independence Day, the Gujarat Forest Department, with technical support from Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre (GZRRC), Vantara, released 20 blackbucks also known as antilope cervicapra, into the Banni Grasslands of Kutch, marking an important milestone in the restoration of native wildlife and the ecological character of this unique grassland landscape.The release comprised five male and 15 female blackbucks, transferred from Vantara, Jamnagar, following the requisite approvals of the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, and the Central Zoo Authority (CZA). The transfer was undertaken in accordance with prescribed protocols covering veterinary examination, health screening, quarantine, disease surveillance, safe and humane transportation and release. Vantara complied with all the necessary requirements.The significance of the initiative extends beyond the release of 20 animals. Restoring native herbivores is an important part of rebuilding the ecological fabric of Banni, strengthening its native herbivore community, supporting natural predator prey relationships and contributing to the recovery of a more resilient grassland ecosystem.Banni is a vast grassland landscape supporting pastoral communities and diverse native wildlife. Blackbuck, chinkara, nilgai and wild boar have historically formed part of its herbivore assemblage. Their recovery, alongside habitat conservation and scientific grassland management, can help restore the ecological character and biodiversity of the landscape.The initiative reflects the broader national commitment to the revival of India’s native species and restoration of its grassland ecosystems, a conservation direction strongly championed under the leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi.Dr Jaipal Singh, IFS, Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, said, “Restoring native wildlife is fundamental to restoring healthy landscapes. The release of these 20 blackbucks into Banni on India’s Independence Day is an important milestone in our continuing effort to recover the ecological character and biodiversity of this unique grasslands. Such restoration requires science, sustained management and collaboration, and we appreciate Vantara’s technical support in carrying out the programme in accordance with prescribed protocols. ”Ajit Kulkarni, Special Director, Compliance & Due Diligence, Vantara, said, “There can be no greater privilege on Independence Day than contributing to a future in which India’s native species continue to live and flourish in the natural landscapes to which they belong. Species restoration is not simply about releasing animals; it requires a thorough understanding of the habitat, the species and the individual animals being released, as well as habitat dynamics, population planning, and the active support of all stakeholders, particularly local communities, to ensure the long term success and sustainability of these efforts. We are honoured to support the Gujarat Forest Department and the Government’s conservation vision for Banni, and to contribute our technical capabilities wherever they can strengthen India’s wildlife conservation efforts.”The Banni release forms part of a wider programme to strengthen native herbivore populations across Gujarat. The Central Government, through the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, has approved the translocation of 500 blackbucks and 100 chinkara, with the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, providing the necessary directions for the exercise.While components of this wider programme support prey base augmentation in connection with the planned cheetah reintroduction programme, the Banni blackbuck release also has an important and independent species restoration objective: rebuilding populations of wildlife native to the grasslands.The Banni Grassland Forest Division has sought Vantara’s technical support for the wider translocation programme, including specialised herbivore transport vehicles, portable boma systems, veterinary expertise and technical support for safe handling and transportation.The initiative builds on the Gujarat Forest Department’s sustained conservation work. With the approval of the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, Vantara has previously supported the Forest Department in the rewilding of nearly 80 spotted deer in Barda Wildlife Sanctuary, contributing to biodiversity strengthening within the Asiatic lion conservation landscape.
Article Summary: 20 blackbucks released into banni grasslands of kutch on india's 80th independence day. Part of a wider gujarat native herbivore conservation programme to strengthen native herbivore populations. Vantara complied with all the necessary requirements to release the animals.

Article Title: 'His personal views': Punjab Congress distances itself from Deepender Hooda over Sajjan Kumar tribute row

NEW DELHI: Punjab Congress leaders on Friday sought to distance the party's state unit from Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda's remarks describing former party MP and 1984 anti-Sikh riots convict Sajjan Kumar as a "role model nationwide". The leaders said the party stood with those who were killed and affected by the violence and that it was Hooda's "personal views".The pushback from Punjab Congress came a day after Sajjan Singh Kumar, who was serving a life sentence in connection with the 1984 riots, died at the age of 84 at Safdarjung Hospital in Delhi.Hooda had described Kumar's death as an "irreparable loss" to the country's political landscape and said he had been a prominent figure whose connect with people was "exemplary".The remarks triggered sharp criticism from Sikh groups, opposition parties and families of riot victims, forcing Congress leaders in Punjab to clarify that Hooda's comments did not reflect their position.Congress MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Kumar had committed "misdeeds", had been punished for them and could not be held up as a model for political leadership."Sajjan Kumar did misdeeds. He has been punished for his actions.A leader does not lead in harming others. We stand with those who died due to him," Aujla said in Amritsar.Asked specifically about Hooda's remarks, Aujla said they should be viewed as the Haryana MP's personal opinion."It must be the personal opinion of Hooda ji but our view is that whatever happened and whoever it happened with, we stand with them, the victims," he said.Punjab Congress working president Raj Kumar Verka also sought to put the focus on the victims of the violence."Sajjan Kumar's life had been full of controversies. This is a matter related to Punjab and Punjabis have been hurt. If Sajjan Kumar is being held responsible for it, we first stand in support of those innocent people; Sajjan Kumar comes only later," Verka said."I don't know who said what. We are Punjabis and we will continue to stand with Punjabis," he added.Congress MP Manish Tewari, however, declined to comment directly on Hooda's statement, saying he had not read it."I haven't read the statement, so it won't be correct to comment on it," Tewari saidHooda's comments came after Kumar's death on Thursday.Speaking to ANI, Hooda described Kumar's death as a loss to the political landscape and praised his public connect."Today, the country's political landscape has suffered an irreparable loss... He is cited as a role model nationwide," Hooda had said.The remarks quickly became controversial given Kumar's conviction in cases related to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, which followed the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi by her Sikh bodyguards.Kumar was a three-time parliamentarian and had faced criminal proceedings over the violence for decades. His legal journey included both acquittals and convictions before higher courts.The BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal sharply criticised Hooda and questioned whether his remarks represented the Congress's broader position.BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu accused Kumar and his associates of systematically targeting Sikh families during the 1984 violence and alleged that the Congress leadership had protected him for years.Bittu called on the Punjab and Delhi Congress units to clarify their position on Hooda's comments.The Shiromani Akali Dal also demanded an apology from Hooda and the Congress.SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia condemned the statement and said Congress should apologise."How can a person like Jagdish Tytler, HKL Bhagat...and all those who killed our innocent Sikh brothers in broad daylight and are responsible for the murder of around 3,000 people during the 1984 riots, be called role models?" Majithia said.He also questioned whether Hooda would continue to remain in the Congress after making the remarks.SAD leader Daljeet Singh Cheema said Hooda should have considered the impact of his comments on families whose homes were destroyed and relatives killed during the violence."When you glorify the life of such people in public, it causes a great deal of hurt to the Sikh community," Cheema said.The president of the 1984 Anti-Sikh Riots Victim Welfare Society, Surjit Singh, also condemned Hooda's remarks, saying victims had still not received justice.The controversy unfolded alongside emotional reactions from families affected by the 1984 violence.Ganga Kaur, a member of a riot-affected family, said members of her family had been killed during the violence."Members of our family were burned alive in front of us. Hospital authorities said he had a history of high blood pressure and Parkinson's disease and had been admitted after being brought to the hospital by police with altered sensorium.Kumar had been serving a life sentence after the Delhi high court in December 2018 overturned his acquittal in the Raj Nagar case, relating to the killing of five members of a Sikh family and the burning of a gurdwara during the 1984 violence.He surrendered and was lodged in Tihar Jail in December 2018.In February 2025, a Delhi court sentenced Kumar to another life term in the Saraswati Vihar case over the killings of Jaswant Singh and his son Tarundeep Singh during the riots.
